public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hyperscalers' AI bets cannot pay off while they keep spending three or more times their annual AI revenue on capex.
conditions: if hyperscalers keep spending 3x+ their AI revenue on capex yearly

statement.excerpt: Put another way, AI bets cannot “pay off” if hyperscalers continue to funnel three or more times their AI revenues every single year into capital expenditures.

from_speaker: three or more times their AI revenues
our_interpretation: Pay off ordinarily means recovering the AI investment through cumulative net cash returns, rather than merely generating revenue or raising the share price.
The antecedent requires annual capital expenditures of at least three times realized annual AI revenue over the continuing investment period.

The surrounding discussion concerns company-wide hyperscaler capex. That is the primary reading of the numerator, while the mismatch between total capex and AI-specific investment must remain explicit.
Revenue, spending, and returns must be compared for the same companies and years. An annualized revenue run rate does not establish realized annual revenue.
The surrounding discussion invokes analyst estimates, so the claim's monetary basis is treated as estimate rather than GAAP.
No deadline or minimum duration for continue is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Once the annual three-times condition is established, complete investment and cash-return records show that the AI investments fail to recover their cost over their economic lives while the condition continues.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show recovery of the AI investment through cumulative net cash returns while annual capex remains at least three times realized annual AI revenue over the relevant continuing period.
